task: Measure W1 checker syntax caching on the optimized C++ compiler.
observation: On the same machine and -O2 build, three alternating baseline/W1 runs of w3_spec_repeated_n032 had median check times 2.5343 s and 1.8371 s; w5_infer_wide_w100 had medians 10.8669 s and 9.0077 s. The W3 profile emitted 9,350,195 parse-cache hits and 1,782,615 misses. Both compilers returned the same check result on these workloads.
impact: The candidate shows a measured gain on repeated-expression workloads; the result still needs full correctness and benchmark gates before W1 can be integrated.

resolution.summary: Paired timing supports the optimization; full W1 acceptance remains in progress.

task: Run the full B1 compiler benchmark before W1.
observation: All 154 one-repetition timing and profiling trials completed, but report generation raised TypeError because checked_specs came from the first timing row, where the profiling-only count was None.
impact: The benchmark command exited unsuccessfully after producing valid raw results; report-only regeneration was needed to retain the baseline without rerunning every workload.

resolution.summary: Aggregation now selects the first populated specialization count; report-only generation succeeded on the completed baseline CSV.

task: Start automated W1 PR regression gates on hosted runners.
observation: The first PR run built compiler objects but failed at link: clang rejected -fuse-ld=mold because the hosted runner did not have mold. The Makefile's local default assumed mold was installed.
impact: The optimized-example job could not reach its test step, so the first PR SHA had no green gate evidence.
evidence: GitHub Actions run 40265968076, optimized-examples job: clang++: error: invalid linker name in argument '-fuse-ld=mold'

resolution.summary: The Phase 26 workflow sets the Makefile's documented empty MOSS_LDFLAGS override. The replacement CI run must still prove the gate.
